aliases: U.S. Navy Office of Naval Intelligence
organizations.normalization_notes: The wartime office remains distinct from the Coordinator of Information and OSS. This is modeled as a military assignment, not civilian employment.
Coster's 1940 ambulance service is modeled as volunteer service, not as civilian employment by the French Army.
Student attendance is kept separate from employment. The contemporary source gives class-year shorthand, not proof of a degree.

affiliations.organization_name_as_found: Office of Naval Intelligence in Washington
affiliations.role_title: Navy member assigned to naval intelligence
affiliations.date_precision: The 1946 account says Coster joined the Navy after returning from France, entered ONI because of his French, and was transferred when Donovan established the Coordinator of Information; exact appointment and transfer dates are not stated.
affiliations.research_notes: This is the best-supported immediate predecessor to Coster's transfer into Donovan's organization. COI was OSS's institutional predecessor; the record does not imply a second recruitment at the June 1942 renaming.

affiliations.date_precision: The November 1940 profile identifies Coster as sales manager of an unnamed Montreal advertising firm; the 1946 chronology calls him an advertising-agency executive before American Field Service ambulance duty early in 1940.
affiliations.research_notes: This is the last identifiable civilian employer before volunteer wartime service and Navy entry. The firm is unnamed, so no organization is invented or normalized.

affiliations.date_precision: TIME names Coster with an American Field Service group near Amiens in late May 1940; his contemporary first-person article and the 1946 chronology independently describe the service.
affiliations.research_notes: This volunteer service intervened between civilian advertising work and Navy/ONI service. It is neither an employer nor the immediate predecessor to Donovan's organization.

affiliations.date_precision: The November 1940 profile prints Princeton '29; it does not separately state a degree or graduation date.
affiliations.research_notes: Princeton is modeled only as a student affiliation and excluded from employer analytics.

affiliations.occupation: Kitchen workers in hotels, restaurants, railroads, steamships, etc., n.e.c.
affiliations.date_precision: The identifier-matched Army statistical card dated 5 August 1942 carries civilian-occupation value 229; the official table defines the broad category.
affiliations.research_notes: The category establishes no employer, workplace, exact duties, work dates or Army-to-OSS sequence.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Donald Q Coster is a high-confidence match to the Princeton '29 advertising executive, 1940 American Field Service volunteer, Navy/ONI member, and Donovan-assigned author documented by contemporary sources.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact name and middle initial recur across the OSS index, Coster's signed 1940 article, a contemporary TIME report, his coauthored 1946 OSS account, and an institutional 1942 Dakar report.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from an uncommon exact full name with middle initial, a coherent Montreal-France-Washington-North Africa chronology, signed first-person articles, and an archival report bearing the same name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources document civilian advertising work before 1940 volunteer service, followed by Navy/ONI service and transfer into Donovan's organization.
claims.match_notes: The indexed six-digit private identifier has not yet been independently linked to these public sources. Box 146 remains necessary for confirmation.

claims.claim_text: A contemporary 1947 trade report describes Donald Q. Coster as having served as an Army colonel during the North African operations.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The report identifies Coster as a former Army colonel while discussing the radio dramatization of his documented North African role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The rare exact name, North African operation, and reference to the Coster story align with the 1946 coauthored account and indexed person.
claims.temporal_assessment: The report was published in 1947 and explicitly describes wartime rank and service.
claims.match_notes: The index rank field is blank. Commissioned status is therefore high confidence, not confirmed from the index alone.

claims.claim_text: Donald Q. Coster's best-supported immediate pre-Donovan affiliation was the U.S. Navy's Office of Naval Intelligence in Washington.
claims.evidence_excerpt: pushed him into the Office of Naval Intelligence
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The coauthored account explicitly sequences Navy entry, ONI assignment, and transfer into Donovan's newly established COI, later OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The signed story, rare exact name, indexed OSS file, and matching Dakar archival record support the identity.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate: the account says he was transferred from ONI into Donovan's new organization.
claims.match_notes: The claim concerns entry into Donovan's organization through COI. It does not recast ONI as a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Before volunteer wartime service, Donald Q. Coster was sales manager of an unnamed advertising firm in Montreal.
claims.evidence_excerpt: sales manager of an advertising firm in Montreal
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A November 1940 profile states the role and city; the 1946 chronology independently calls him an advertising-agency executive before his 1940 ambulance service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The same rare exact name and middle initial appear in the signed article and indexed OSS record; the later coauthored account supplies the continuous chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the last identified civilian employment before American Field Service duty early in 1940.
claims.match_notes: The firm is not named. No employer name is inferred from Coster's later postwar advertising work.

claims.claim_text: Donald Q. Coster drove an American Field Service ambulance in France in 1940 before returning to the United States and joining the Navy.
claims.evidence_excerpt: American Field Service men, led by Donald Q. Coster
claims.evidence_paraphrase: TIME reported the exact-name AFS group near Amiens in June 1940; Coster's contemporary article and the 1946 account corroborate the ambulance service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact rare name, Montreal context, signed first-person account, and continuous 1946 service narrative support the match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to 1940 and explicitly before Navy and ONI service.
claims.match_notes: Modeled as volunteer service rather than employment by the French Army.

claims.claim_text: A contemporary 1940 profile identifies Donald Q. Coster with Princeton's class-year designation 1929.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The profile places the class-year shorthand directly beside Coster's full name and occupation.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact rare name and middle initial, signed article, Montreal occupation and AFS context align with the indexed person and later OSS account.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar student affiliation; degree completion is not asserted.
claims.match_notes: Princeton is excluded from employer analytics.
